capabilities: show a per-section bar rail on notes with at least three headings
preview a section's content on hover, pointer sweep, or keyboard focus
jump to a heading by click, Enter, or command palette
configure the minimum heading count and enable the rail in Reading view or Live Preview
disambiguation: Not a bookmarking or note-linking tool; it only navigates sections within a single note.
extras: Local-only by design: reads headings and excerpts, stores only its own settings, and makes no network requests or analytics calls. Previews intentionally omit embeds, images, fenced code, tables, HTML, and display math. The manifest notes it has not been manually reviewed by Obsidian staff.
intentEvidence: inspired by the elegant table-of-contents affordance used for long conversations
motivation: The author was inspired by the table-of-contents affordance used for long conversations in other apps.
problem: Long notes make the built-in outline cumbersome; there is no compact in-page affordance for seeing and jumping between sections without leaving the text.
summary: Heading navigation rail that shows a stack of bars on the note edge, with hover previews of each section and click or keyboard jumps.
